title: Python Functions: Return Values
description: Practice reading and writing small functions. The questions assume you know variables and basic expressions.

questions.prompt: What does a return statement do inside a function?
options: Sends a value back to the caller
Defines another function with the same name
Stops the caller before it receives a result
questions.correct: Sends a value back to the caller
questions.explanation: return ends the current function call and gives its value back to the code that called the function.
The call supplies 3 and 4 for the two parameters, and the function returns their sum.

questions.prompt: A function with no value-bearing return statement returns None by default.
questions.explanation: When execution reaches the end of a function without returning a value, Python returns None.

questions.prompt: Which line correctly calls a function named greet?
questions.explanation: Parentheses after a function name make a call. def defines the function rather than calling it.
The argument Maya is joined to the greeting string and returned.

questions.prompt: In def double(number), what is number?
questions.explanation: A parameter is the named input a function receives when it is called.
Because 2 is greater than zero, the first return runs and the later return is skipped.

questions.prompt: The same function can be called more than once with different arguments.
questions.explanation: A function is reusable; each call gets its own parameter values and local execution.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes a user-defined function?
options: A reusable block of code with a name
A value that can only be text
A file that must be downloaded
questions.correct: A reusable block of code with a name
questions.explanation: def creates a named, reusable block that can accept inputs and return a result.
The function multiplies its input, 4, by 3 and returns 12.
